active_themes.label: Warsh's Credibility Collapse
active_themes.summary: Hammack's 'rate hikes, not cuts' warning is now validated by real-time macro data: 3.4% inflation with zero spending growth cannot accommodate policy loosening. Warsh's intellectual case for cutting into stagflation has no remaining empirical support. The Fed is fractured because there is no good answer. Today's 172K jobs + flat wages confirm the bind: the labor market has not broken enough to justify cuts, but cutting anyway (as Warsh implied) would worsen inflation dynamics. Warsh's only path to credibility now is public capitulation—a statement that rate hikes remain on the table. Until that happens, markets will assume policy error and reprice accordingly.

active_themes.label: Iran Escalation Resumes
active_themes.summary: After the Israel-Lebanon ceasefire announcement (June 2), Iran has launched drone attacks toward the Strait of Hormuz and the US has struck Iranian radar sites. This is a clear signal that the ceasefire does not resolve the US-Iran dimension of the conflict. Oil remains modestly elevated but has not spiked, suggesting markets are pricing a contained escalation rather than full disruption. The 72-hour window for either a formal US-Iran deal or a collapse in negotiations is now active. A deal would give Warsh a brief reprieve but does not solve the core stagflation problem. A collapse pushes oil toward $95 and forces equities down further.

active_themes.label: Lenders Silent Through Jobs Report
active_themes.summary: Discover, Capital One, and Amex had maximum cover today to announce deposit rate cuts or consumer credit tightening—flat May spending, stagflationary backdrop, Hammack's dominance over Fed policy. They remained silent, which on its surface is surprising. This silence will not hold beyond 3-7 days. The institutional delay is now the narrowest open window in the repricing chain. When the first major lender moves, it will be a cascading signal: credit is tightening, demand is weakening, and equities are mispriced for that reality.

active_themes.label: Soft Landing Officially Dead
active_themes.summary: May's 0% MoM spending combined with today's institutional silence removes all remaining soft-landing narrative credibility. Equities have not repriced this yet. The repricing cycle begins when the first lender announces tightening, expected in the next 3-7 days.

active_themes.label: Yields Stuck at Stagflation Range
active_themes.summary: 10-year remains 3.9-4.1%; 30-year at 2007 highs. Hammack's warning and today's spending data validate stagflation scenario. Yields will not move lower without hard demand destruction (not evident) or inflation rollover (not happening). This is the correct price for an economy cutting rates while inflation stays elevated.

active_themes.label: Bond Market Vindicated
active_themes.summary: The bond market has correctly priced stagflation since May 15 (10-year stuck at 3.9–4.1%, 30-year at 2007 highs). Today's sell-off confirms bonds were leading: equities are now repricing the same scenario. A 4.18% Nasdaq decline is the beginning of the reset, not the end. The repricing accelerates when credit tightening is announced and becomes undeniable—3–5 more percent downside in equities is built into the base case over the next 2-3 weeks.
